title: Steiner introduces Squirrel Ashcraft and the interview aims
summary: Steiner introduces Ashcraft as a Chicago-style bandleader and says the interview will cover New Orleans influence on Chicago and New York.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: For those who may listen to this tape, my name is John Steiner. I want to introduce Edwin Ashcraft, Squirrel Ashcraft, who's been a leader in Chicago of the Chicago-style jazz bands, both amateur and professional. And his name will be familiar to anyone in our generation who has been acquainted with the Chicago Fellows. Squirrel has played and recorded with people like Freeman and McPartland. He knew Teschmacher and knew well that Davy Tuff and Krupa has played on many occasions with the Condon gang and is currently active, as he has been for the last 30 or 40 years. I thought from a squirrel's position that he might talk with an objectivity and an unconcern about the sources of inspiration for the Chicago Fellows. And that would catch a great deal of the New Orleans influence in its first stage on its arrival to Chicago and what it did to Chicago. He then was able to observe what it did to New York. He tells me that in about 1925, when he was at school in the East, he began to visit New York and see what the popular music picture was there. He was particularly interested in the jazz aspects, and that took him close to New Orleans influences. Squirrel, would you tell us a little bit about where you were born and when and your parents and brother and sister and that sort of thing, just so that we have you identified?
